title: Rome Turns East
objective: After this level you can describe how Rome came to dominate Greece and the Hellenistic kingdoms.
summary: Rome beat Macedon and came to control Greece, destroying Corinth in 146 BCE. Meanwhile Greek culture conquered Rome from within.

cards.headline: Rome conquered Greece. Then Greece conquered Rome right back.
cards.body: Rome won the wars in the east. Greek art, books and ideas won over the Romans.

cards.headline: Wars with Macedon
cards.body: In the east, Rome’s opponent was the kingdom of Macedon. In a series of wars ending in 148 BCE, Rome came to control Greece. Along the way, in 196 BCE, the Roman general Flamininus proclaimed the Greek cities free. Free, on paper. Roman influence over them only kept growing, like a guest who says he’s just visiting and keeps unpacking.

cards.headline: Captive Greece
cards.body: Then the conquered started conquering back. Greek art, literature and philosophy deeply shaped Roman culture, changing how Romans made art, wrote and thought about the world. The poet Horace put it perfectly: captive Greece took its fierce conqueror captive. Rome took the land. Greece took the Romans, one statue and one book at a time.

cards.context: The Greek cities’ freedom had limits. In 146 BCE Rome destroyed the Greek city of Corinth. Hold on to that year: in the same year, Rome destroyed Carthage too.
